title: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF Is Near Its All-Time High: Is It Still a Good Buy?
author: David Jagielski, Cpa
description: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) has surged 22% this year and hit an all-time high, prompting questions about valuation. Despite the gains, the ETF maintains a reasonable price-to-earnings multiple of less than 20 (below the S&P 500's 23) and offers a 3% dividend yield, making it still attractive for income-focused investors seeking safety and quality dividend stocks.

title: Veeva Expands Amgen Partnership With Global Vault CRM Rollout Plan
author: Na
description: Veeva Systems announced that Amgen has selected its Vault CRM platform for global deployment, extending their partnership of over a decade. The deal reinforces Veeva's commercial business momentum, with the company reporting its best CRM quarter ever, 180+ live Vault CRM customers, and confidence in maintaining over 70% market share in life sciences CRM. The global healthcare CRM market is projected to grow at a 6.2% CAGR from 2026 to 2033.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Major enterprise validation from Amgen's global deployment decision, best CRM quarter ever reported, 180+ live customers, strong market share position (70%+), commercial subscription revenue growth of 13% YoY, and expanding AI-enabled capabilities driving adoption among large pharmaceutical companies.

The selection of Vault CRM is a positive operational decision for modernizing commercial operations and accelerating therapy delivery, but the article focuses primarily on Veeva's perspective rather than Amgen's financial or strategic implications.

title: Psoriatic Arthritis Market Landscape: 6 Key Late-Stage Drugs Set to Drive Future Growth | DelveInsight
author: Delveinsight
description: The psoriatic arthritis market is expected to expand significantly through 2036 driven by emerging late-stage therapies from major pharmaceutical companies. Key drugs in development include tildrakizumab (Sun Pharma), sonelokimab (MoonLake), icotrokinra (Johnson & Johnson), zasocitinib (Takeda), izokibep (Affibody Medical), and vunakizumab (Suzhou Suncadia). These novel biologic and oral small-molecule therapies aim to address unmet needs among patients with inadequate responses to existing treatments.
